item.title: Ranji Trophy: Tanush Kotian takes career-best 8-81 as Mumbai secure third bonus point win
item.description: Mumbai: Off-spinner Tanush Kotian produced a career-best 8-81 and an impressive match haul of 11-151 as Mumbai crushed Haryana by 10 wickets on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash at the MCA ground. The win gave Mumbai their third successive bonus-point victory of the season, marking their best start in a long time. They now have 21 points from three matches - the most among all teams in the Ranji Trophy - and sit atop their group, firmly placed on the road to the knockouts. Mumbai will next take on Railways at the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India from November 2-5. The match will remain special for Kotian, who was playing his 50th first-class game. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket match haul and his fourth five-wicket haul. Chasing a modest target of 97, Mumbai openers Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Saxena completed the job in just 10.4 overs. Raghuvanshi, riding high after scoring his maiden first-class century in the first innings, smashed an unbeaten 67 off 39 balls. Saxena, who had struggled in his previous two innings, made a confidence-boosting 30 not out off 25 balls. The final day, however, was not entirely straightforward for Mumbai. Haryana's eighth-wicket pair of Samant Jakhar and Anuj Thakral made the hosts toil on a slow surface, adding 81 runs over nearly two hours. Kotian eventually broke the stand by bowling Jakhar. Haryana, who had resumed on 73-2, still 87 runs behind after following on, were bowled out for 256 in the second session. Reflecting on Mumbai's strong start to the season, Kotian said, "As a team, we've worked well. It's very difficult to get a third victory with a bonus point. Everyone is backing each other and giving confidence. We're trying to contribute together. If the team goal is going well, we want to keep moving forward like this." Brief scores: Mumbai 430 & 97-0 (Raghuvanshi 67*). Haryana 270 & (following-on) 256 (Kotian 8-81) Mumbai won by 10 wickets. Points: Mumbai 7, Haryana 0. 135351570

item.title: Predicting Purdue football's road game at Penn State
item.description: UNIVERSITY PARK, Pennsylvania − Purdue football isn't quite in desperation mode, but it certainly feels like Saturday's game at Beaver Stadium is a must have. The Boilermakers want to play football beyond the 12-game regular season and travel to Penn State with a 3-4 record. The remaining schedule is daunting, making a game against a team that's 0-4 in the Big Ten one of epic proportions in hopes of ending a four-year bowl-less drought. The Boilermakers are certainly capable of trick-or-treating their way to victory on Halloween, but it will take a more impressive performance than Purdue 's most recent, a 38-26 loss to Washington on Oct. 16. The Nittany Lions have won 11 straight meetings since Purdue's 2004 victory at Penn State. Scouting Purdue football's opponent, Penn State The Matt Campbell era started off well and good. Penn State opened the non-conference portion of its schedule outscoring Marshall, Temple and Buffalo by a combined score of 127-22. Then Big Ten play began and the Nittany Lions haven't won since, suffering setbacks in league play to Wisconsin, Northwestern, USC and Michigan. Penn State ranks 17th in the Big Ten in red zone defense, but overall has the ninth ranked defense, mostly to the credit of its pass defense. Sacks: Rojas (5). Interceptions: Rojas (2), Josiah Zayas (2). Kicking: Ryan Barker (11-13 FG, long of 48, 21-21 PAT). Punting: Nathan Tiyce (31 punts, 41.1 average). In recent years, though, Allen's method has proven to be more sustainable. item.title: Liverpool get irresistible Alexis Mac Allister offer from Real Madrid
item.description: Liverpool get irresistible Alexis Mac Allister offer from Real Madrid That’s according to a new report in Fichajes which claims the 27-year-old Argentine is Los Blancos’ top transfer target for winter 2027. Mac Allister joined the Reds back in 2023 from Brighton for a bargain fee of around £35m. The No10 has since established himself as one of the best midfielders in the world - roaring back into form this season under Andoni Iraola. The 2022 FIFA World Cup winner is only contracted until 2028 and so far contract talks have not been fruitful. Mac Allister is Madrid's top target Mac Allister was hurt by Liverpool’s reluctance to offer him a new deal - while Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch got their contracts extended at considerable expense. With less than two years left on his contract Liverpool’s sporting director Julian Ward will soon be forced into a decision over Macca. Either face up to losing him for free in 2028 - should no deal be done - or else sell him for a decent fee in 2027. No doubt the 2024/25 Premier League champions would insist on a big fee for Mac Allister - which Real Madrid are already aware of. Accordingly the 15-time European champions are trying to entice Liverpool into a deal by exchanging one of THREE named players for Mac Allister. TAA, Brahim and Camavinga offered to Liverpool The report claims Trent Alexander-Arnold could be one of the names offered to the Reds with the 28-year-old’s time in the Spanish capital so far proving to be an unhappy stint. Then there’s Brahim Diaz - a long-term Liverpool link who has struggled to establish himself under Jose Mourinho. And rounding out the list is Eduardo Camavinga - a dynamic and progressive No6 who has yet to nail down a starting spot under the Special One. item.title: Germany Frauen to play Argentina and Peru in November friendlies
item.description: BREMEN, GERMANY - OCTOBER 13: Klara Buehl of Germany celebrates with Melissa Koessler, Linda Dallmann, Janina Minge Franziska Kett, Elisa Senss and Cora Zicai (L-R) of Germany after scoring her team's second goal during the Women's international friendly match between Germany and Japan at Weser Stadium on October 13, 2026 in Bremen, Germany. (Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Germany Frauen will be going across the Atlantic Ocean for their last international break of the year. The DFB announced that the women’s national team will be flying to South America in the November/December international break. This is presumably to get acclimated to the local scene, as next year’s World Cup will be held in Brazil. Speaking of Brazil, Rio de Janeiro will play host to Germany’s second friendly of the break, which will be against Peru. Four days before then, Germany will play Argentina on their home turf in La Plata. The Argentina game will be played on the last day of November. Germany have only faced Argentina twice in their history, winning both games 6-1 and 11-0. However, since their last game was nearly 20 years ago in 2007, the results will most likely matter very little. Meanwhile, this will be their first ever meeting with Peru. The last time Germany played South American opponents was back at the 2023 World Cup, when they lost 1-2 to Colombia. Join the conversation! His status and superstar’s salary can come with a responsibility. Grealish let David Moyes and Everton down. They responded by lifting themselves up. item.description: One of the top events on the high school basketball calendar is moving to Carmel High School this season. The annual Hope Plumbing Tipoff Classic is set for Dec. 12 and will feature six games, including one state champion and a runner-up from last season and several teams that should be top contenders in their respective classes this season. A closer look at the six games: Barr-Reeve vs. Blackford, noon Barr-Reeve is the reigning Class 1A state champion, coming off a 28-1 season last year in Heath Howington’s first year as coach. The Vikings have reason to believe they can repeat with several returners, including senior Kierson Lengacher (14.0 ppg, 2.4 assists) and juniors Jaylon Graber (10.8 ppg, 4.0 rebounds), and Braxton Neidigh (9.9 ppg, 3.3. rebounds). Blackford is coming off a 20-7 season and Class 2A sectional title and brings back one of the most talented players in the state in junior Amarian Leggett (26.3 ppg, 4.3 assists, 4.2 rebounds). Eli Petro, a 6-8 senior, will be a key player for the Bruins. Austin vs. Oak Hill, 1:30 p.m. There are high expectations for both of these Class 2A programs. Oak Hill, which went 25-2 last year and won a regional title, had one of the highest-scoring teams in the state last year and should again be one of the state’s top teams. Senior Jace Tonagel (16.0 ppg, 6.0 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 2.6 steals) returns with sophomore younger brother Will Tonagel (14.4 ppg, 3.7 assists, 2.6 steals) and several other key players, including seniors Kevaunte Simmons (8.3 ppg, 3.3 rebounds) and Jayden Younce (6.1 ppg, 4.0 rebounds). Austin had a major breakthrough last year, winning a Class 2A regional title and finishing 17-9. Indiana recruit Micah Mohler is coming off an outstanding freshman season that saw him average 21.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.1 assists. Junior guard Tracen Roush (14.7 ppg, 3.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists) is another player to watch for Austin. Crown Point vs. Zionsville, 3 p.m. Crown Point loses a lot to graduation from last year’s Class 4A state runner-up team, but does bring back one of the top juniors in the state in 6-4 guard M.J. Wilson (8.5 ppg, 2.2 rebounds) and 6-8 senior Cooper Malaski (5.0 ppg, 4.0 rebounds). The Bulldogs finished 25-2 last season. Crnjar has confirmed that the Uruguayan is settled at Anfield and pleased with his contribution to the team, leaving the possibility of a permanent move or a return to Camp Nou open. The 27-year-old’s loan move to Liverpool has provided an important opportunity to rebuild his confidence and rediscover his best football. item.title: Watch: Yan Diomande glides past Real Madrid players in training with utmost ease
item.description: Watch: Yan Diomande glides past Real Madrid players in training with utmost ease The Real Madrid squad’s confidence is at its highest since the start of the season after Sunday’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona. Many players have been responsible for sparking this remarkable turnaround, and one of them is Yan Diomande. After taking a few weeks to settle in at his new club, the Ivory Coast winger is getting better and better with each passing game. The 19-year-old winger has once again demonstrated his extraordinary dribbling ability in training, producing two outstanding individual moves against his Madrid team-mates. Diomande leaves Madrid teammates chasing shadows In the first sequence, Diomande receives possession and immediately accelerates into a crowded area, effortlessly weaving past three or four teammates. His close control is particularly impressive, allowing him to change direction repeatedly without losing momentum or letting defenders get close enough to challenge. The second sequence is arguably even more spectacular. Starting from the right flank, Diomande takes on Marc Cucurella, producing a sharp move that leaves the Spanish defender on the ground. He then cuts inside and unleashes a beautiful curling effort into the far corner, completing a wonderful individual goal. Such moments offer another glimpse of why Madrid invested so heavily in the youngster’s potential. His speed is exceptional, but his ability to manipulate the ball in tight spaces makes him especially difficult to contain. Mourinho has an exciting attacking weapon Diomande’s performances this season suggest his training-ground brilliance is translating into competitive football. Diomande is growing at Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Ahead of the Clasico , he was averaging 4.88 successful dribbles per 90 minutes in La Liga , having contributed two goals and two assists in 457 minutes. Against opponents defending deep, Diomande can create openings through individual skill and add another threat to Madrid’s attack. More importantly for Jose Mourinho, the Ivorian has also shown that he is willing to track back and support his full-back. The youngster’s confidence seems to be skyrocketing, and he will hope to perform along the same lines against Racing Santander this weekend. It remains to be seen how Diomande’s role changes after Vinicius Jr. comes back into the fold and whether the two star wingers can coexist in the same system.

item.title: Tadhg Furlong cleared of grabbing opponent’s groin by disciplinary panel
item.description: The Leinster and Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cleared by a disciplinary committee after an allegation that he grabbed the groin of Munster ’s Gavin Coombes during a United Rugby Championship (URC) game. Coombes alleged during Munster’s 24-18 defeat at the Aviva Stadium that he had been grabbed at a ruck, but the television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find conclusive video evidence after a referral from referee Andrew Brace. Furlong was subsequently cited, though, under Law 9.27 , which states "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals". On Thursday, however, the 33-year-old was cleared of sanction at a hearing, leaving him free to feature in Ireland’s Nations Championship games in November. “Having reviewed all of the evidence and considered the submissions in this case, the Independent Disciplinary Committee unanimously concluded that the citing complaint against the Player should be dismissed, on the basis that he did not commit an act of foul play contrary to Law 9.27,” a URC statement said. “Notwithstanding the dismissal of the complaint, the Independent Disciplinary Committee found that Munster No 8, Mr Gavin Coombes, had given an honest account of his recollection of events surrounding the incident, and that the Citing Complaint was properly brought before the Independent Disciplinary Committee for determination.”

item.title: Richard Sherman Sends Candid Jonathan Taylor Message to Seahawks
item.description: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have made one big move ahead of the trade deadline, trading for the Indianapolis Colts‘ Quenton Nelson. Nonetheless, former Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman believes that Seattle shouldn’t stop there. In their Week 7 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, the Seahawks showed that they have the defense that can carry them to another Super Bowl. Now, the question is: Can they get more production from the offense? Seattle’s passing game has Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the go-to guy, but in the running game, could the Seahawks make a move to bolster that group? Sherman would like the team to do just that before the trade deadline. As for what player the Seahawks should target, Sherman sees Colts’ Jonathan Taylor as the ideal trade option for Seattle. “I think a team they’ve already made a trade with, the Seattle Seahawks, would be in the mix for Jonathan Taylor as well,” Sherman said in an Oct. 29 video from “The Richard Sherman Podcast.” “I’m sure John Schneider and Ed Dodds are having those conversations right now about what it would take. “I’m guessing it would take a Day 1 pick and maybe a little bit more to get Jonathan Taylor out of Indianapolis. He’s the guy who could help this team the most. Everybody needs great running backs, but they need one really badly.” What Would Jonathan Taylor Bring to Seahawks Offense? Taylor has played 319 total snaps for the Colts this season, leading to a 65.3 overall PFF grade . Moreover, he has carried the ball 140 times for 587 rushing yards and eight touchdowns while averaging 4.2 yards per attempt on the ground and forcing 16 missed tackles as a runner. In the passing game, Taylor has caught 17 passes on 24 targets for 178 receiving yards. The question will be whether the Seahawks will want to give up the draft assets for this production, given that they have Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price nearing their returns. Nonetheless, if the Seahawks feel that Taylor can elevate their offense to another level, then perhaps they make this type of deal. Colts Might Not Want to Trade Jonathan Taylor Meanwhile, the latest update from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter suggests that the Colts want to hold onto their star running back, or at least it might be a hint that they haven’t received an offer that would cause them to trade him yet. “The big name is Jonathan Taylor, and my understanding is that the owner doesn’t want to trade him,” Schefter said during an Oct. 27 appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” “We have two weeks until the deadline. I’m sure they don’t want to trade Jonathan Taylor, and if I had to guess today, I would say I don’t think they will trade him. “I think there are going to be teams out there that are interested and will try to have conversations and make offers. If the Colts don’t change their stance, they won’t trade Jonathan Taylor. Again, I think the owner doesn’t want to trade him right now, for the record. That doesn’t mean it won’t happen.

item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes driver George Russell reckons Ferrari has "quite an advantage" at F1's Mexican Grand Prix with its turbo design, while Charles Leclerc still believes Mercedes has the best car "wherever we go". Mexico's capital megalopolis sits on a 2250m plateau, which gives the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez one of the most unique engineering challenges. The lower-density air reduces aerodynamic performance and has major cooling headaches, but it may also reward Ferrari for some of the design decisions it made with its 2026 power unit. Boasting a smaller diameter turbocharger compared to its rivals, the turbo's lower inertia allows it to spool up quicker, which has a compound effect when the air is much thinner at altitude and there is less exhaust energy available to begin with. The trade-off is a limit on peak horsepower compared to larger diameter turbines. "I think it's going to be very interesting. I think turbo lag is going to be a big factor for a lot of teams this weekend," Russell pointed out. "There's obviously no secret that the likes of Ferrari have a smaller turbo than most, so they probably have quite an advantage in this regard. We're not sure as yet how challenging it will be, but I can definitely foresee it being not straightforward." Ferrari's Leclerc was quick to play down his team's favourite tag, coming after a series of wins for Max Verstappen in the significantly improved Red Bull and a victory in Austin for champion-elect Kimi Antonelli in the Mercedes. Ferrari, which also introduced significant upgrades last weekend, hasn't won a grand prix since Leclerc triumphed at July's British Grand Prix in Silverstone. item.title: Chiefs coach talks up Harrison Butker’s windy practice prowess with Justin Tucker hovering over him
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Chiefs coach talks up Harrison Butker’s windy practice prowess with Justin Tucker hovering over him appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker delivered a perfect practice performance despite facing difficult conditions and new competition. The impressive response came after Kansas City signed veteran Justin Tucker to its practice squad following Butker’s recent struggles. Special teams coordinator Dave Toub said Butker made all 10 kicks during Wednesday’s practice, despite wind gusts reaching 28 mph. Tucker watched nearby as the veteran kicker responded to mounting pressure. “He went 10-for-10 yesterday with Tucker standing right there,” Toub said, according to ESPN’s report. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Toub emphasized that Butker remains Kansas City’s preferred kicker despite the decision to add competition. “We’re trying to improve and get Butker right,” Toub said. “That’s what this whole thing is about. He’s our kicker.” Butker has converted just 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. His struggles included two misses during Sunday’s 20-3 defeat against the Seattle Seahawks. The veteran missed attempts from 58 and 45 yards, contributing to Kansas City’s disappointing offensive performance against Seattle. Meanwhile, Tucker impressed during his workout with Kansas City, converting all 30 attempts. His performance included seven kicks beyond 50 yards and one from 60. Toub also revealed that both kickers have exchanged advice about technique and handling difficult situations. Their conversations could help Butker regain his consistency. Kansas City faces the Denver Broncos on Sunday in a crucial AFC West matchup. Butker is expected to retain his starting role. However, Tucker’s presence gives the Chiefs another option should their longtime kicker continue struggling. For now, Butker’s flawless performance under windy conditions provides encouraging evidence that he can respond to the competition. A handful of accounts had noticed that on various betting websites, Chelsea’s likelihood of scoring multiple goals had been steadily dropping since 10am. Their probability of winning the game was falling too. Then there were the fantasy football sleuths. An account called “Team news and ticks” is well known for its reliable leaks, and it posted: “Some massive assets [players] missing in multiple games today,” in a direct call to the FPL community. Given there were only three more games that day, and Chelsea were the most popular team for fantasy managers, it raised the possibility of an injury among their supreme front three: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro . Then came the real investigative work. An account called FPL Joe posted a diagram analysing the fantasy football teams of individuals closely linked to the Chelsea dressing room, featuring players, staff and family members. Then again, had the game been on Sunday or Monday night, Tottenham would have had plenty of time to prepare for Chelsea’s possible line-ups. That scenario would not have pleased Alonso, who is highly secretive when it comes to team news, to the point where journalists who regularly cover the club can find themselves with very little to write about after pre-match press conferences. Alonso even refused to reveal Joao Pedro’s injury in September, before the last international break, despite the striker having already been ruled out by Brazil. After Tottenham’s 2-0 win at the weekend, the Chelsea manager was asked whether he was bothered by the inadvertent leak from inside the club. “I am not into the fantasy team thing, so I didn’t know that,” Alonso replied. Xabi Alonso prefers to stay tight-lipped about team news (Getty) It is not unusual for Premier League team news to slip out on social media, particularly in the fantasy football community, where knowledge is power. Five years ago, the FPL’s weekly transfer deadline was moved back by half an hour to combat leaks which were giving an unfair advantage to those fantasy managers glued to the right social media accounts in the minutes before the deadline fell. The situation came to a head at Aston Villa during that 2020/21 season when an account called FPL Insider posted that five people inside the Villa dressing room, including some first-team players and a club physio, had transferred Jack Grealish out of their fantasy teams. The news surfaced on social media more than 24 hours before kick-off in their Premier League match against Leicester City, and Leicester manager Brendan Rodgers admitted he had learnt about the reports of Grealish’s injury well ahead of the game. It’s something I wouldn’t be happy with and we’ll get to the bottom of it.” Villa players and staff were banned from playing fantasy football as a result of the incident. But after a week in which the manager’s secretive bubble was seemingly breached, employees at Cobham might be taking a little more care ahead of this weekend’s game Premier League game against Manchester United.

ESPN's "College GameDay" attempts to travel to some of the most marquee matchups each and every week. ESPN does not explain its decision on where the show travels to every week, nor does it have to. But the decision to go to Bloomington feels like a curious one. Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that." Challenged over why she carried on, she said: "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect." The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was "traumatic". She also said she had considered walking away from the sport, in which she holds a world record. Hyrox sees participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing, and lunges while carrying a sandbag. The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, in northern Germany, and is now held across the world. Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning [Getty Images] Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea. item.title: Orange basketball - Brand encouraged with improvements by the women
item.description: Sixth-year head coach Micah Brand is very encouraged about the women's basketball team he's assembled at SUNY Orange. With six sophomores and five talented freshmen (and a potential for a couple more additions from the volleyball team), Brand says "this is probably the best I felt about a group I've had,'' since he took over the head coaching reins. Brand figures the Colts will be more competitive and should produce more offense this season, which gets underway Sunday at SUNY Broome. Orange is coming off a 5-18 campaign, with a 2-2 mark in the Mid-Hudson Conference. The Colts should benefit from having a handful of "older'' players. Cornwall center Grace Breheny, a 2024 high school grad, averaged eight points, is a top-flight rebounder and earned all-region honors. Eldred's Jada Reed, who graduated in 2018 and later served in the National Guard, averaged 8.2 points, bringing energy and intensity to the small guard role, alternating at point. Tianna Kirton from Brooklyn - a 2011 high school graduate - has shifted from her job as an assistant coach to a starting guard role, able to hit shots. A pair of freshmen recruits should fill the other two starting spots: guard Mariah Kinscy from Ellenville sees the floor well, can share the point duties, plays with good pace and was a BCANY high-school all-star; and forward Gianna Pacciarelli was a three-year starter for Monroe-Woodbury and the Crusaders' defensive player of the year (she also played soccer and lacrosse), bringing poise and good court sense. Likely first off the bench will be Mariah Diaz, Mia Domingues and Madison Olsen. The freshman Diaz played four seasons for Middletown, bringing rebounding and running ability. Domingues is a good shooter, was a BCANY all-star and played on two Section 9 championship teams at Wallkill - she is coming off an injury and should resume full duties soon. Minisink Valley grad Olsen has good basketball IQ and averaged 10.2 points last season. Brand hasn't married himself to just one type of style, and believes he adjusts well to the talent he's been given. He says this team can run a bit - more to his liking - but also slow down when needed. He is hopeful of an improved defensive performance, and would like for his team to set the tone more often. Last season, Orange often scored in the 40s; Brand believes this team has the talent to score closer to 60 on a regular basis. item.title: Micah Parsons’ Packers return could take longer than expected as NFL insider shares update
item.description: Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images Micah Parsons could be back at Green Bay Packers practice soon, but an NFL insider has warned that his return to game action may take longer than fans hope. Speaking on Amazon Prime’s broadcast, James Palmer explained that the Packers intend to take a careful approach as the All-Pro edge rusher works his way back from injury. Parsons has missed the opening eight games of the 2026 NFL season, leaving Green Bay without one of its most important defensive players. Head coach Matt LaFleur recently offered fresh hope that the 27-year-old could return to practice ahead of Week 9, although the final decision rests with the team’s medical staff. James Palmer warns Green Bay Packers fans to be patient with Micah Parsons’ recovery Palmer reported that an official decision on Parsons’ practice return could come early next week, with the expected move marking the beginning of a gradual process. “No official decision has been made. That’s going to happen Monday or Tuesday, I’m told,” Palmer said. He added: “But this is a big step expected for him, and the start of the ramp-up period that they’re going to have within practices. I’m told they are going to go through a proper process, and Chris, it may be a moment before he is back on a playing field during a game.” Palmer stressed that Green Bay wants Parsons to be fully ready before he returns, suggesting the Packers are unlikely to rush him into action. That approach would fit with comments from Parsons’ brother, Terrance, who previously suggested the defensive star could spend at least three weeks practising before playing again. Even if Parsons returns to practice next week, that would not guarantee his availability for the Packers’ Week 9 meeting with the New England Patriots. Week 10 against the Minnesota Vikings remains a possible target, but the team’s Week 11 bye makes a return against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12 a more realistic possibility. Green Bay will be keen to have Parsons available for the closing stretch of the season as it looks to strengthen its playoff hopes. For now, the immediate priority is getting him back onto the practice field without risking another setback. item.description: The biggest night in Everton’s season started with a big call from David Moyes and demanded a big performance from his players. With the exception of Jack Grealish , they did not let him down. A quarter-final at Fleetwood Town is their prize after a clinical, committed display shattered Newcastle’s hopes of lifting the Carabao Cup for a second time in three seasons. Newcastle dominated spells of the fourth round tie and the stats – registering 28 shots to Everton’s 11, although only nine visiting attempts were on target – but individual defensive errors and an ineffective attack proved a ruinous combination. Matthias Jaissle denied his team are a soft touch, despite persuasive evidence to the contrary, yet called Newcastle “naive” and the defeat, in front of almost 8,000 of their fans, “shocking”. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.content:encoded: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
